then: Ibn Kathir says this is a promise to the children of Adam, male or female, who do righteous deeds with belief. Scholars explained the good life as lawful provision, contentment, happiness, and joy in obeying Allah; {reward}the correct view is that it includes all of these.{/reward} He cites the hadith: {idea}successful is the one who submits, has enough, and is made content with what he is given.{/idea}
now: Your friend has the bigger car and the bigger salary and still can't sleep. Your aunt has a small flat, prays on time, and laughs easily. {reward}A good life is not measured in square meters.{/reward}
old: A good life means having a lot.
new: A good life is faith, good deeds, and being content with what Allah gives.
try: Say tonight, out loud: I am content with what Allah has given me today.

title: Before you recite the Quran, seek refuge from Shaytan.
subtitle: Guarding the mind before reading
then: Ibn Kathir says this is a command for those about to read the Quran. {idea}The reason is that the reader should not get confused{/idea}, and that {trap}Shaytan would not stop him from thinking about and pondering the meaning{/trap} of what he reads.
now: You sit down to read the Quran and suddenly remember an email, a message, a snack. Five minutes later you're on your phone. {trap}The distraction is not random.{/trap} {idea}Seeking refuge is asking for focus.{/idea}
old: Saying a'udhu billah is just a formality.
new: Seeking refuge before reading protects my focus from Shaytan.
try: Next time you read Quran, say a'udhu billah slowly and mean it, then put your phone in another room.

title: Shaytan has no power over those who believe and rely on Allah.
subtitle: Trust in Allah is a real protection
then: Ibn Kathir reports Ath-Thawri's view: {idea}Shaytan has no power to make them commit a sin they will not repent from.{/idea} Others said he has no argument over them. It follows the command to seek refuge before reciting the Quran.
now: You slip into the same sin again and think, I'm hopeless, he always wins. {reward}The verse says the believer who relies on Allah can always come back.{/reward} He can trip you; he cannot stop you repenting.
old: Shaytan is stronger than me.
new: With faith and trust in Allah, Shaytan cannot keep me from returning.
try: After your next slip, make tawbah immediately instead of waiting.

title: His hold is only on those who take him as an ally.
subtitle: Shaytan's power is borrowed from the one who follows
then: Mujahid said his authority is over {trap}those who obey him{/trap}, and others said {trap}those who take him as their protector instead of Allah{/trap}, and those who associate partners with Allah. Ibn Kathir places this right after the believers' protection.
now: You keep the app that leads you into wrong, you keep the friend who always pulls you toward it, you keep the late-night habit. {idea}Each one is an open door.{/idea} His power grows when you keep following.
old: Shaytan just takes over sometimes.
new: Shaytan's power over me grows only as far as I follow him.
try: Close one door today: delete one app, mute one chat, or change one routine that leads you to sin.

title: When a ruling was replaced, they called the Prophet ﷺ a forger.
subtitle: Allah knows best what He sends down
then: Ibn Kathir says when the idolators saw some rulings changed, {trap}they said to the Messenger ﷺ: you are a forger.{/trap} But {idea}Allah is the Lord who does what He wills and rules as He wants.{/idea} Mujahid explained it as removing one verse and putting another in its place.
now: Your doctor changes your medication once you're through the first phase. You don't call her a liar. {idea}The one who knows the whole plan can change a step.{/idea} Allah knows best what His servants need and when.
old: If something in religion changed, it can't be from Allah.
new: Allah knows best what to send and when, and a change is His wisdom.
try: Next time something in the deen confuses you, say Allah knows best and ask a scholar.

title: Jibril brought it with truth, to make believers firm.
subtitle: The source of the Quran and its purpose
then: This answers the forger accusation. Ibn Kathir says Ruh-ul-Qudus is Jibril, who brought it {idea}with truthfulness and justice{/idea}, so that believers {reward}believe what was revealed earlier and what was revealed later, and humble themselves to Allah.{/reward}
now: Someone online tries to shake you with clips claiming the Quran contradicts itself. {idea}The verse says the Quran came to make you firm, not shaky.{/idea} Return to the source and to people of knowledge.
old: Every doubt I hear might bring down my faith.
new: The Quran came from my Lord with truth to make me firm.
try: Read one passage of the Quran today with the intention of being made firm.

title: They said a man teaches him, a man who barely spoke Arabic.
subtitle: An accusation that falls apart on its own
then: Ibn Kathir says the idolators pointed to {trap}a non-Arab servant who sold goods by As-Safa{/trap}. The Prophet ﷺ may have sat and talked with him a little, but the man knew only simple Arabic phrases. {idea}How could the Quran, with its eloquent style and perfect meanings, come from him?{/idea}
now: When you want to dismiss something, you grab any explanation, even one that makes no sense. A colleague's success? Must be connections. {trap}A rushed accusation often says more about us than them.{/trap}
old: If I can find any explanation, I don't have to accept it.
new: An explanation that makes no sense is just a way to avoid the truth.
try: Before you dismiss something today, ask if your reason would convince a fair person.

title: Those who refuse His signs are left without guidance.
subtitle: Guidance needs a heart that wants it
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah does not guide {trap}those who turn away from remembering Him, who are heedless, and who have no intention of believing.{/trap} Such people will not be guided by the signs, because they never wanted to be.
now: You say you want to change, but you avoid every talk, every reminder, every friend who might push you. {idea}Guidance comes to those who want it.{/idea} Wanting it starts with not running from it.
old: If Allah wanted me guided, it would just happen.
new: Guidance meets those who turn toward it; refusing it closes the door.
try: Make a sincere dua today: O Allah, make me want what You want for me.

title: The liars are the ones who invent lies, not Al-Amin.
subtitle: The Prophet ﷺ was known for honesty
then: Ibn Kathir says the Prophet ﷺ {reward}was known among his people for his truthfulness; they called him Al-Amin.{/reward} When Heraclius asked Abu Sufyan if they ever accused him of lying before his claim, Abu Sufyan said no. Heraclius reasoned: {idea}would he refrain from lying about people, then lie about Allah?{/idea}
now: Your record is your witness. The coworker who never fudges a timesheet is believed when it matters. {reward}Small daily honesty builds the trust that speaks for you later.{/reward}
old: Little lies don't affect my credibility.
new: A track record of honesty is what makes people trust my word.
try: Go a full day without a single exaggeration or white lie.

title: Forced words with a heart at peace in faith are excused.
subtitle: The heart decides, not words under torture
then: Persecution in Makkah was at its height when this came. Ibn Kathir describes the one who {idea}says words of disbelief under beatings and abuse while his heart refuses them.{/idea} He mentions Bilal, who under {trap}a huge rock on his chest in the heat{/trap} kept saying: Alone, Alone.
now: You may never face torture, but you face pressure: the joke you laugh along with to fit in, the silence when your faith is mocked. {idea}Your heart knows the difference between being cornered and choosing.{/idea} {reward}Bilal's courage is a light for smaller tests.{/reward}
old: Only my words show what I believe.
new: Allah sees the heart; and steadfastness under pressure is precious.
try: Next time your faith is mocked in a small way, say one calm, kind word for it.

title: They preferred this world over the Hereafter.
subtitle: The root reason for leaving faith
then: Ibn Kathir says these people {trap}understood the faith yet still turned away from it{/trap}, because they preferred this life to the Hereafter. They {trap}left the faith for the sake of this world.{/trap}
now: A job offer that requires you to drop your prayers. A relationship that pulls you away from Allah. {idea}The trade is rarely presented as leaving faith. It is presented as a good deal.{/idea}
old: I can always balance this world and my faith later.
new: When I put this world above the next, I start to drift from faith.
try: Look at one big decision you're weighing and ask: what does it cost my akhirah?

title: Hearts, ears and eyes sealed: they became the heedless.
subtitle: Senses that no longer help
then: Earlier in the surah, hearing, sight and hearts were listed as gifts for gratitude. Ibn Kathir says here Allah {trap}put a seal on their hearts so they would not understand what benefits them{/trap}, and sealed their ears and eyes. {trap}Their faculties did not help them at all.{/trap}
now: You hear the Quran in the car and it doesn't land. You watch a funeral pass and feel nothing. {idea}Numbness is a warning sign, not a resting place.{/idea} {reward}A heart can be softened while it still beats.{/reward}
old: Feeling nothing at reminders is just how I am.
new: A heart that stops responding needs care before it hardens further.
try: Sit with one verse of the Quran today until something in it moves you.

title: No doubt, in the Hereafter they are the losers.
subtitle: The final result of choosing this world
then: Ibn Kathir says la jarama means it is inevitable that those who are like this {trap}will lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection.{/trap} This closes the passage about those who traded faith for the world.
now: You track wins: the promotion, the new car, the followers. {idea}Picture the final scoreboard, where only one column counts.{/idea} Losing yourself is the only loss that cannot be recovered.
old: As long as I'm winning here, I'm doing fine.
new: The real loss is losing myself in the Hereafter, whatever I gain here.
try: Write one line tonight: what am I building that will still count on that Day?

title: They gave in under trial, then emigrated and endured. He forgives.
subtitle: A way back for those who once broke
then: Ibn Kathir says this refers to people {trap}oppressed in Makkah, whose position was weak, who went along with their people when tried.{/trap} Then they escaped, leaving homeland, families and wealth, joined the believers and bore hardship with patience. {reward}Allah tells them He will forgive and show mercy.{/reward}
now: You gave in once, badly. Maybe you left prayer for years, or did something you can't say out loud. {reward}This verse is for people who fell and then got up and kept going.{/reward} What you do after counts.
old: Once I've failed that badly, there's no way back.
new: Allah forgives those who fall, then turn, strive and stay patient.
try: Take one concrete step back toward Allah today from a place where you once fell.

title: Every soul comes pleading for itself, and no one is wronged.
subtitle: Alone with your record, and full justice
then: Ibn Kathir says each person will make a case in his own defense, {trap}no one else will plead for him: not father, son, brother or wife.{/trap} Each will be paid for what he did, good or evil, {idea}with no decrease in reward and no increase in punishment.{/idea}
now: You rely on being part of a good family, a good mosque, a good group. On that Day you'll stand on your own. {reward}Every quiet good deed you did will be there, none missing.{/reward}
old: My family and community will carry me through.
new: I will stand for myself, and every good I did will be counted exactly.
try: Do one good deed today that no one else will ever know about.

title: A safe, well-fed town denied His favors and tasted hunger and fear.
subtitle: The example of Makkah
then: Ibn Kathir says this is the example of Makkah, {reward}a secure sanctuary while people outside were being snatched away.{/reward} They denied Allah's favors, the greatest being the Prophet ﷺ sent to them. When they insisted on opposing him, {trap}they were struck with years of famine{/trap}, and their security turned to fear.
now: Your city is safe, your shops are full, the lights always come on. It's easy to forget that these are favors. {idea}Gratitude is how you hold on to what you have.{/idea}
old: Safety and plenty are just normal.
new: Safety and plenty are favors that need gratitude to last.
try: Thank Allah today, by name, for the safety of your home and the food in your kitchen.

title: A Messenger came from among them, and they denied him.
subtitle: The greatest favor, rejected
then: Ibn Kathir says this happened because of {trap}their rejection of the Messenger ﷺ that Allah sent to them from among themselves.{/trap} He reminds of the verses calling this a blessing: a Messenger {reward}reciting His verses, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom.{/reward}
now: You have the Sunnah at your fingertips: his words, his manners, his prayers, all a search away. {idea}A favor ignored is a favor slowly lost.{/idea}
old: The Prophet's ﷺ example is nice but not urgent for me.
new: The Prophet ﷺ is one of the greatest favors given to me.
try: Learn one sunnah today and practice it before the day ends.

title: Eat what is lawful and good, and be grateful.
subtitle: After famine, an invitation to eat and thank
then: Right after the example of the town that tasted famine, the verse turns to believers. Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}orders His believing servants to eat the good and lawful things He provided and to give thanks{/idea}, for He is the Giver of all favors and alone deserves worship.
now: Lunch at your desk, eaten while scrolling, barely tasted. {idea}The same meal eaten with bismillah and alhamdulillah becomes worship.{/idea}
old: Meals are just fuel.
new: Eating good and lawful food with thanks is a way of worshipping Allah.
try: Eat one meal today without your phone, starting with bismillah and ending with alhamdulillah.

title: Only a few things are forbidden, and need finds mercy.
subtitle: A short list and a wide door
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah mentions what He forbade, {trap}things which harm people in both religious and worldly affairs.{/trap} Yet if someone is forced by need, without deliberately disobeying, {reward}Allah is Pardoning, Most Merciful.{/reward}
now: Sometimes faith feels like a long list of no. Read the verse again: {idea}a handful of limits on one side, a whole world of good food on the other.{/idea} And mercy for real need.
old: Religion is mostly about what I can't have.
new: Allah made the good wide and the forbidden few, with mercy for need.
try: Name five good foods you enjoy, and thank Allah for each.

title: Don't let your tongue declare halal and haram from your whim.
subtitle: Inventing rules and putting Allah's name on them
then: The idolators had invented sacred camels like the Bahirah and Sa'ibah with no revelation behind them. Ibn Kathir says this verse includes {trap}whoever declares something lawful that Allah forbade, or forbidden that He permitted, only because it suits his opinion or whim.{/trap} Those who invent lies against Allah will not succeed.
now: Someone at dinner says, that's definitely haram, with total confidence and no source. Another says, it's fine, Allah doesn't mind. {trap}Both are speaking for Allah without knowledge.{/trap} {idea}It is fine to say: I don't know, let me ask.{/idea}
old: I can say what's halal or haram based on how it feels.
new: Only Allah sets halal and haram; I speak about it only with knowledge.
try: Next time you're about to call something halal or haram, check your source first or say I don't know.

title: A brief enjoyment, then a painful end.
subtitle: What lying about Allah really buys
then: This follows the warning about inventing halal and haram. Ibn Kathir says they {trap}will never succeed, either in this world or the Hereafter. In this world it is transient pleasure{/trap}, then the return is to Allah.
now: Bending a rule to make life easier feels great for a while: the shortcut, the convenient opinion. {trap}It is short.{/trap} {idea}What you gain from twisting the truth runs out faster than you think.{/idea}
old: If it makes my life easier now, it's worth it.
new: Comfort bought by twisting Allah's words is brief and ends badly.
try: Drop one convenient opinion today that you hold only because it suits you.

title: Stricter rules for an earlier people, and they wronged themselves.
subtitle: Ease for this ummah, by contrast
then: Ibn Kathir says after allowing ease in necessity, {reward}part of making things easy for this ummah, because Allah desires ease for us{/reward}, the verse mentions what was forbidden to the Jews in their law, as related in Surat Al-An'am. {idea}Allah did not wrong them; they wronged themselves.{/idea}
now: You complain that the deen is hard, then remember how much is open to you, and that need brings mercy. {reward}You've been given ease.{/reward} {idea}The question is whether you meet ease with gratitude or with carelessness.{/idea}
old: My religion is too strict on me.
new: Allah made my way easy; my own wrongs are what make life hard.
try: List three ways your faith makes life easier, and thank Allah for them.

title: Did wrong in ignorance, then repented and corrected: He forgives.
subtitle: A door held open for every sinner
then: Ibn Kathir says this honors believers who have sinned: {reward}whoever repents, He will accept his repentance.{/reward} Some of the Salaf said {idea}everyone who disobeys Allah is ignorant{/idea}, so this includes all sinners who give up their sins and turn to obedience.
now: You knew it was wrong and did it anyway, so you think this verse isn't for you. {idea}Scholars said every sin is a kind of ignorance.{/idea} {reward}The door is open to you too.{/reward} Repent, then fix what you can.
old: I knew better, so there's no forgiveness for me.
new: Every sin is ignorance, and my Lord forgives those who repent and reform.
try: Pick one sin, make sincere tawbah tonight, and replace it with one good habit tomorrow.

title: Ibrahim was a nation on his own, obedient and upright.
subtitle: One man who stood for Tawhid
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah praises Ibrahim, {idea}the Imam of the Hanifs and father of the Prophets.{/idea} Ummah means a leader who is followed; Mujahid said {reward}he was a nation on his own.{/reward} Qanit means humble and obedient; Hanif means deliberately steering clear of shirk.
now: You're the only one in your office who prays, the only one in your friend group who doesn't drink. {reward}Ibrahim stood alone too, and Allah called him a nation.{/reward}
old: Standing alone for my faith makes me odd.
new: One person upright before Allah can be a whole nation in His eyes.
try: Do one act of faith today openly where you'd usually hide it.

title: Grateful for His favors, so Allah chose and guided him.
subtitle: Gratitude and being chosen
then: Ibn Kathir says Ibrahim {idea}gave thanks for the blessings Allah gave him{/idea}, linking it to the verse calling him the one who fulfilled, meaning {idea}he did everything Allah commanded.{/idea} Allah chose him and guided him to worship Him alone.
now: This surah has listed favor after favor: rain, cattle, honey, homes, senses. Ibrahim is the picture of the person who actually said thank you, with his whole life. {reward}You can be that person.{/reward}
old: Gratitude is a feeling.
new: Gratitude is doing what Allah asks with the gifts He gave.
try: Turn one blessing into action today: use your health to pray or your money to give.

title: Good in this world, and among the righteous in the next.
subtitle: What Ibrahim was given
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {reward}granted him all that a believer needs for a good and complete life in this world.{/reward} Mujahid said the good was {reward}a truthful tongue{/reward}, meaning he is remembered with honor. In the Hereafter he is among the righteous.
now: Thousands of years later, millions say Ibrahim's name in every prayer. {reward}That is the good name Allah gave him here.{/reward} {idea}How will people speak of you after you're gone?{/idea}
old: Living for Allah means giving up a good life here.
new: Allah can give good in this world and the next to those who live for Him.
try: Do one thing today you would want to be remembered for.

title: The Prophet ﷺ was told: follow the way of Ibrahim.
subtitle: The final Messenger follows the upright father
then: Ibn Kathir says because of {idea}Ibrahim's perfection, greatness, and the soundness of his Tawhid{/idea}, Allah revealed to the Seal of the Messengers ﷺ to follow his way. He links it to the verse: a right religion, the religion of Ibrahim, a Hanif.
now: When you pray, you send blessings on Ibrahim and his family in the final sitting, by name. {idea}You're standing in a line that goes all the way back.{/idea}
old: My faith is just what my family happens to do.
new: My faith is the path of Ibrahim, carried by the Prophet ﷺ to me.
try: In your next prayer, pay attention to Ibrahim's name in the salawat and thank Allah for the line you're in.

title: Each nation got a day of worship; we were guided to Friday.
subtitle: A day given, and those who differed over theirs
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah prescribed a weekly day of worship for every nation, and for this ummah {reward}Friday, the day He completed His creation.{/reward} The Sabbath was for those who differed over it. He quotes the Prophet ﷺ: {idea}we are the last, but we will be the first on the Day of Resurrection.{/idea}
now: Friday arrives and it can feel like any workday: emails, a rushed lunch, Jumu'ah squeezed in. {reward}It is a gift this ummah was guided to.{/reward} {idea}Treat it like one.{/idea}
old: Friday is just another day with a prayer in the middle.
new: Friday is a day Allah guided me to; it deserves my care.
try: This Friday, arrive early for Jumu'ah and read some Quran before the khutbah.

title: Invite with wisdom and good words; argue in the best way.
subtitle: How to call people to Allah
then: Ibn Kathir says if anyone wants to debate, it should be {idea}with kindness, gentleness and good speech{/idea}, as Allah told Musa and Harun to speak mildly even to Pharaoh. Then: {reward}do not exhaust yourself with regret over those who go astray{/reward}, for guiding them is not your task.
now: Your uncle makes a provocative comment about religion at a family dinner. You could win the argument and lose him. {idea}Speak gently, the way Musa was told to speak even to Pharaoh.{/idea}
old: Winning the argument is how I defend my faith.
new: I invite with wisdom and gentleness, and leave guidance to Allah.
try: In your next disagreement about faith, lower your voice and say one kind thing first.

title: If you respond, keep it equal. Patience is better.
subtitle: Justice as the limit, patience as the higher choice
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}Allah commands justice in punishment and fairness in settling rights.{/idea} Ibn Sirin said if someone takes something from you, take something similar. Ibn Zayd said some strong new Muslims wanted to strike back at the idolators of Makkah, and this came. Then the verse adds: {reward}patience is better.{/reward}
now: Your coworker took credit for your work in the meeting. Your hand is already typing a long email to the whole team. {idea}A fair response is allowed.{/idea} {reward}Patience is the better road, and it is rewarded.{/reward}
old: If someone wrongs me, I should hit back harder.
new: I may answer a wrong fairly, but patience is better.
try: Wait 24 hours before responding to the next person who wrongs you.

title: Be patient; your patience comes only from Allah.
subtitle: Don't grieve or be squeezed by their plots
then: Ibn Kathir says this {idea}tells us patience cannot be gained except by the will, help, decree and power of Allah.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ is told not to grieve over those who oppose him or be distressed by their plots, {reward}for Allah is protecting, helping and supporting him.{/reward}
now: You're running out of patience: with the kids, the landlord, the neighbor who keeps complaining. {idea}Stop trying to squeeze more out of yourself.{/idea} {reward}Ask the One who gives it.{/reward}
old: I just need to try harder to be patient.
new: Patience is something I ask Allah for, not only something I force.
try: When patience runs low today, pause and say: O Allah, grant me patience.

title: Allah is with those who are mindful and do good.
subtitle: The closing promise of the surah
then: Ibn Kathir says this is {reward}a special kind of being with: supporting, helping and guiding.{/reward} He cites the Prophet ﷺ in the cave saying to Abu Bakr: {idea}do not worry, Allah is with us.{/idea} Allah is with everyone by knowledge and sight, but with these by care. So ends Surat An-Nahl.
now: You walk into the job interview, the hospital room, the hard conversation, feeling alone. {reward}If you stayed away from wrong and tried to do good, you're not alone in there.{/reward}
old: I'm on my own when things get hard.
new: Allah is with those who are mindful and do good, helping them.
try: Before your next hard moment, whisper: Allah is with me, and do one good deed.
